chapters.title: Unit 1: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH), The Rasool of Mercy

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Glossary — Word Meanings

  • Q: Meaning of 'foster-mother':
    Ans: A woman who takes another person's child into her home for a period of time, without becoming his or her legal parent.
  • Q: Meaning of 'widow':
    Ans: A woman whose husband has died.
  • Q: Meaning of 'proposal':
    Ans: An act of formally asking somebody to marry you.
  • Q: Meaning of 'orphan':
    Ans: A child whose parents are dead.
  • Q: Meaning of 'AD':
    Ans: Anno Domini, a Latin phrase meaning 'in the year of the Lord', which is used when referring to the year after Hazrat Essa (AS) was born.
  • Q: Meaning of 'slave':
    Ans: A person who is legally owned by someone else and has to work for that person.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Why was Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) called Sadiq and Amin?
    Ans: Since childhood, Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) was loved and respected by all. He never told a lie, so people called him 'Sadiq', the truthful one. He was always honest and fair in his dealings with people, so people also called him 'Amin', the trustworthy one.
  • Q: Q2. Why is Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) called Rahmatul-lil-Aalamin?
    Ans: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) was kind, gentle and merciful to everyone. He loved the poor, treated orphans and widows with kindness, helped the slaves and the helpless, was kind to birds and animals, and treated even his enemies with kindness. His mercy was for all, so he is called Rahmatul-lil-Aalamin, a mercy for all the worlds.
  • Q: Q3. What was the impact of Hazrat Muhammad's (PBUH) personality on people?
    Ans: People loved and respected Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) from his childhood because he never told a lie and was always honest and fair. Hazrat Khadija was so pleased with his honesty and truthfulness that she wished to marry him. He won the hearts of his friends and enemies by love, kindness and mercy, and not by force.
  • Q: Q4. What are the worst sins in the eyes of Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)?
    Ans: Note: This question is printed in the book, but the lesson text on pages 2 to 4 does not list any sins, so no answer can be taken from this lesson. The lesson only teaches that we should never tell a lie, never treat anyone unkindly, and always be honest, fair, kind and merciful to all.
  • Q: Q5. How did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) win the hearts of his enemies and friends?
    Ans: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) won the hearts of his friends and enemies by love, kindness and mercy, and not by force. In the battle of Hawazin he set free as many as 6,000 prisoners of war, and when Makkah was conquered he forgave all his enemies. At Taif, when he was wounded by stones, he refused to curse his enemies and said he had been sent to be a mercy to mankind.

Comprehension — B. Circle the correct article (a / an / the)

  • Q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) was looked after by ______ foster mother.
    Ans: a
  • Q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) never told ______ lie.
    Ans: a
  • Q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) was kind to ______ poor slaves.
    Ans: the
  • Q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) was ______ grandson of Hashim.
    Ans: the
  • Q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) treated ______ rich and ______ poor alike.
    Ans: the / the

mcqs.q: Why was Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) called 'Sadiq'?

Because he was honest in his dealings

mcqs.q: Why was Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) called 'Amin'?
options: Because he was kind to animals
Because he never told a lie
Because he was always honest and fair in his dealings with people
Because he helped an old man carry water
mcqs.why: The notes say he was always honest and fair in his dealings with people, so people called him 'Amin', the trustworthy one.

mcqs.q: Why is Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) called Rahmatul-lil-Aalamin?
options: Because he was the grandson of Hashim
Because his mercy was for all — he was kind to the poor, orphans, widows, slaves, animals and even his enemies
Because he lived with his uncle Abu Talib
Because he was brought up by a foster-mother

mcqs.q: What did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) do at Taif when he was wounded by stones?

He refused to curse his enemies and said he had been sent to be a mercy to mankind
He left Taif and never returned
mcqs.why: The notes say that at Taif, though wounded by stones, he refused to curse his enemies and said he had been sent to be a mercy to mankind.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — A. Find the meaning of the following words in the dictionary and identify the part of speech

  • Q: Meaning and part of speech of 'modest':
    Ans: Modest (adj. = adjective) means humble and not proud; in the lesson, women should be good and modest, that is, decent and humble in dress and behaviour.
  • Q: Meaning and part of speech of 'pardon':
    Ans: Pardon (v. = verb) means to forgive someone for a wrong. In the lesson: 'If they do wrong, pardon them.'
  • Q: Meaning and part of speech of 'pitied':
    Ans: Pitied (v. = verb, past tense of pity) means felt sorry for someone in trouble. In the lesson, Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) pitied the old man who carried water and helped him.
  • Q: Meaning and part of speech of 'conquer':
    Ans: Conquer (v. = verb) means to take control of a place or country by force. In the lesson, when Makkah was conquered, Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) forgave all his enemies.
  • Q: Meaning and part of speech of 'curse':
    Ans: Curse (v. = verb) means to wish harm or evil upon someone. At Taif, Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) refused to curse his enemies.
  • Q: Meaning and part of speech of 'mercy':
    Ans: Mercy (n. = noun) means kindness and forgiveness shown to someone instead of punishment. The lesson says his mercy was for all.

Vocabulary — B. Consult a thesaurus and find out the synonyms of the following words

  • Q: Synonym of 'path':
    Ans: Way, road, track.
  • Q: Synonym of 'enemy':
    Ans: Foe, opponent, rival.
  • Q: Synonym of 'kind':
    Ans: Gentle, caring, generous, merciful.
  • Q: Synonym of 'right':
    Ans: Correct, true, proper.
  • Q: Synonym of 'carry':
    Ans: Bear, lift, take, bring.
  • Q: Synonym of 'friend':
    Ans: Companion, mate, well-wisher.

Grammar — A. Replace the underlined common noun (phrase) with a proper noun

  • Q: Q1. The boy went to the city in the morning.
    Ans: Akram went to Peshawar in the morning. (Given in the book as the example.)
  • Q: Q2. The animal in the zoo was very big.
    Ans: The elephant in the Peshawar Zoo was very big.
  • Q: Q3. This boy/girl is my best friend.
    Ans: Ali is my best friend.
  • Q: Q4. We went to the hospital to see the doctor.
    Ans: We went to Lady Reading Hospital to see Dr. Ahmad.
  • Q: Q5. My country is very beautiful.
    Ans: Pakistan is very beautiful.
  • Q: Q6. We will have holidays in the sixth month.
    Ans: We will have holidays in June.

Grammar — B. Underline the nouns and say whether they are countable or uncountable

  • Q: Q1. I turned on all the fans.
    Ans: Noun: fans — countable. (Given in the book.)
  • Q: Q2. Have you found a house yet?
    Ans: Noun: house — countable.
  • Q: Q3. That garden is beautiful.
    Ans: Noun: garden — countable.
  • Q: Q4. The noise frightened her.
    Ans: Noun: noise — uncountable.
  • Q: Q5. There is no light.
    Ans: Noun: light — uncountable.
  • Q: Q6. The iron door has rusted.
    Ans: Nouns: iron — uncountable; door — countable.

Grammar — C. Use one word to classify the bold group of words. Differentiate between countable and uncountable noun

  • Q: Q1. He sells roses, daisies and marigolds.
    Ans: He sells flowers. (Countable — given in the book.)
  • Q: Q2. You can buy pens, pencils, papers and books from his shop.
    Ans: You can buy stationery from his shop. (Countable items; stationery as a class word is uncountable.)
  • Q: Q3. After her operation, she could only have milk, juice or tea.
    Ans: After her operation, she could only have drinks. (Uncountable.)
  • Q: Q4. The carpenter carried his hammer, chisel, and screwdriver.
    Ans: The carpenter carried his tools. (Countable.)

Grammar — D. Write the plurals of the following words

  • Q: Plural of 'raspberry':
    Ans: raspberries
  • Q: Plural of 'sofa':
    Ans: sofas
  • Q: Plural of 'pencil':

  • Q: Plural of 'horse':
    Ans: horses
  • Q: Plural of 'office':
    Ans: offices
  • Q: Plural of 'chimney':
    Ans: chimneys
  • Q: Plural of 'star':
    Ans: stars
  • Q: Plural of 'inch':
    Ans: inches
  • Q: Plural of 'story':
    Ans: stories

    Ans: matches

Grammar — E. Change the following sentences into the plural form

  • Q: Q1. There is a new boy in my class.
    Ans: There are new boys in our classes. (Given in the book.)
  • Q: Q2. A boy helped me find a taxi to go home.
    Ans: Two boys helped us find taxis to go home.
  • Q: Q3. There is a table in Adnan's room.
    Ans: There are tables in Adnan's room.
  • Q: Q4. Sara said that her leg was aching.
    Ans: Sara said that her legs were aching.
  • Q: Q5. A farmer has bought a tractor.
    Ans: The farmers have bought tractors.
  • Q: Q6. A leader should lead by example.
    Ans: Leaders should lead by examples.

Grammar — F. Change these irregular singular nouns to plural nouns and then use them in sentences of your own

  • Q: Q1. Child
    Ans: Plural: children. Sentence: The children are going on a picnic. (Given in the book.)
  • Q: Q2. woman
    Ans: Plural: women. Sentence: Women should be treated with kindness and love.
  • Q: Q3. mouse
    Ans: Plural: mice. Sentence: Three mice ran out of the hole.
  • Q: Q4. tooth
    Ans: Plural: teeth. Sentence: We should brush our teeth daily.
  • Q: Q5. goose
    Ans: Plural: geese. Sentence: The geese are swimming in the pond.
  • Q: Q6. louse
    Ans: Plural: lice. Sentence: Lice live in dirty hair.

Grammar — G. Collective nouns: think of nouns that go with them

  • Q: A fleet of ______.
    Ans: ships (also: cars)
  • Q: A litter of ______.
    Ans: puppies (also: cubs)
  • Q: A bouquet of ______.
    Ans: flowers
  • Q: A pride of ______.
    Ans: lions
  • Q: A herd of ______.
    Ans: cattle (also: elephants, sheep)
  • Q: A swarm of ______.
    Ans: bees

Grammar — H. Think of suitable collective nouns for the following groups of animals and things

  • Q: A ______ of newspaper.
    Ans: bundle (also: heap, pile)
  • Q: A ______ of beads.
    Ans: string
  • Q: A ______ of trees.
    Ans: forest (also: grove, clump)
  • Q: A ______ of birds.
    Ans: flock
  • Q: A ______ of cubs.
    Ans: litter

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — A. Complete the mind map and summarize the lesson with the help of the mind map

  • Q: Q1. Complete the mind map of Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) and write the summary of the lesson.
    Ans: Mind map — Centre: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH). Branches: (1) Childhood: born on 20th April, 571 A.D.; father Abdullah died before his birth; looked after by foster-mother Haleema till the age of five; mother died when he was six; then lived with grandfather Abdul Muttalib and later with uncle Abu Talib. (2) Sadiq and Amin: never told a lie and was always honest and fair, so people called him Sadiq and Amin; Hazrat Khadija married him for his honesty. (3) The Prophet of mercy: kind, gentle and merciful; loved the poor, orphans, widows, slaves and the helpless; fed the hungry even if he himself went without food. (4) Respect for women and kindness to animals: treated women and slaves with kindness and love, and advised kindness to animals. (5) Mercy for enemies: freed 6,000 prisoners at Hawazin, forgave the people of Makkah, and refused to curse the people of Taif. Summary: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) was the greatest and the last Prophet of Allah, born on 20th April, 571 A.D. He lost his father before his birth and his mother at the age of six, and was brought up first by his foster-mother Haleema, then by his grandfather and then by his uncle Abu Talib. He was truthful and honest, so he was called Sadiq and Amin. He was kind and merciful to the poor, the orphans, the widows, the slaves, women, animals and even his enemies, and he won everyone's heart by love and kindness, not by force. That is why he is called Rahmatul-lil-Aalamin, a mercy for all the worlds.

mcqs.why: The mind map's Childhood branch and the summary both state that Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) was born on 20th April, 571 A.D.

chapters.title: Unit 2: New Boy in Class

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Glossary — Word Meanings

  • Q: Meaning of 'wheel chair':
    Ans: A chair fitted with wheels for use as a means of transport by a person who is unable to walk.
  • Q: Meaning of 'scared':
    Ans: Frightened / alarmed.
  • Q: Meaning of 'realized':
    Ans: Understood.
  • Q: Meaning of 'respectful':
    Ans: Showing or having respect.
  • Q: Meaning of 'society':
    Ans: The aggregate of people living together in a more or less ordered community.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Have you ever felt empathy for anyone? When and Why?
    Ans: Yes, I felt empathy for Naseebullah, the new boy in the story, when he came to class in a wheelchair. I understood how he must have felt in a new class, so I wanted to be kind and gentle towards him and make him feel at home, just as the teacher in the story asked the class to do.
  • Q: Q2. What do you feel when you see a child who can't find anyone to play with?
    Ans: I feel sad for such a child and I feel like going to him and inviting him to play with me. Empathy is the ability to understand and share the feelings of another person, so I would not leave him alone; I would include him in our game and make him feel happy.
  • Q: Q3. Have you helped a differently abled person? How?
    Ans: Yes, I have helped a differently abled person. Once I helped a boy in a wheelchair by giving his wheelchair a little push to get over a bump, and I rolled it up the ramp for him, because a wheelchair cannot go up the stairs.
  • Q: Q4. Describe your feelings when you see an animal being hurt.
    Ans: I feel sad and angry when I see an animal being hurt, because animals also feel pain. Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) advised a camel driver to be kind to his animal, so we should stop the person, protect the animal, and treat every animal with kindness.
  • Q: Q5. If Naseebullah were in your class, how would you improve Naseebullah's school experience?
    Ans: I would welcome Naseebullah warmly, introduce myself, and talk to him at recess so that he feels at home. I would include him in our games in the playground, help him with a little push over a bump when he needs it, and use the ramp with him instead of the stairs. I would never tease or bully him, because when we put ourselves in another person's shoes, we become more sensitive to his feelings.

Comprehension — B. Choose correct meaning of the underlined words

  • Q: Q1. As his wheelchair could not go up the stairs, he always rolled it up the special ramp at school. (Choose the correct meaning of 'rolled it up': a. turn up, b. try, c. ignore, d. miss)
    Ans: 'Rolled it up' means he moved / wheeled his wheelchair up the special ramp, because the wheelchair could not go up the stairs. Note: none of the four printed options (a. turn up, b. try, c. ignore, d. miss) gives this meaning, so the correct meaning is given here in words.
  • Q: Q2. We are more familiar with other people's feelings, if we have empathy. (Choose the correct meaning of 'familiar')
    Options: unaware / ignorant / aware of / unconscious
    Ans: aware of
  • Q: Q3. If we are more conscious of other people's feelings, we can create a respectable society. (Choose the correct meaning of 'conscious')
    Options: aware / separate / split / unattached
    Ans: aware
  • Q: Q4. It was a delicate situation. (Choose the correct meaning of 'delicate')
    Options: difficult / easy / sensitive / fragile
    Ans: sensitive

Comprehension — C. State whether the following statements are true or false

  • Q: Q1. Bullying is the way friendly people behave.
    Ans: False — Bullying is unkind behaviour; friendly people are kind and gentle towards others.
  • Q: Q2. Real friends are always helpful and kind.
    Ans: True
  • Q: Q3. True friends always bully.
    Ans: False — True friends never bully; they are helpful and kind.
  • Q: Q4. Bad attitude towards others is a disability.
    Ans: True
  • Q: Q5. Differently abled people do not need care.
    Ans: False — Differently abled people need care, support and empathy from a caring community.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Reading — Deduce the meaning of the following words

  • Q: Q1. Deduce the meaning of 'strong'.
    Ans: Strong means powerful and able to bear hardship. In the poem, a people become 'great and strong' through the hard work and good character of their men, not through wealth.
  • Q: Q2. Deduce the meaning of 'suffer'.
    Ans: Suffer means to bear pain, trouble or hardship patiently for a long time. The poem says men who stand fast for truth and honour 'suffer long'.
  • Q: Q3. Deduce the meaning of 'truth'.
    Ans: Truth means honesty and the quality of being true and right. In the poem, great men stand fast 'for truth and honour's sake'.
  • Q: Q4. Deduce the meaning of 'great'.
    Ans: Great means noble, outstanding and important. In the poem, only good men, not gold, can make a people 'great and strong'.
  • Q: Q5. Deduce the meaning of 'lift'.
    Ans: Lift means to raise something to a higher position. In the poem, brave men build a nation's pillars deep and 'lift them to the sky'.
  • Q: Q6. Deduce the meaning of 'deep'.
    Ans: Deep means going far down below the surface. In the poem, brave men build a nation's pillars deep, that is, they lay a strong and lasting foundation for the nation.

Glossary

  • Q: Q1. What does 'honour' mean?
    Ans: Honour means self-respect.
  • Q: Q2. What does 'stand fast' mean?
    Ans: Stand fast means standing firmly / resolute.
  • Q: Q3. What does 'fly' mean?
    Ans: Fly means run in fear.
  • Q: Q4. What does 'dare' mean?
    Ans: Dare means show courage.
  • Q: Q5. What does 'pillars' mean?
    Ans: Pillars means foundation.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What kind of men can lift their country to the sky?
    Ans: Brave, truthful and honourable men can lift their country to the sky. They are the men who stand fast and suffer long for truth and honour, who work while others sleep and dare while others fly in fear.
  • Q: Q2. What is the main message of the poem "A Nation's Strength"?
    Ans: The main message of the poem is that a nation does not become great and strong by gold or wealth. Only brave and honest men of character, who work hard and sacrifice for their country, make a nation great and strong.
  • Q: Q3. Write the qualities of a brave man.
    Ans: A brave man is truthful and honourable. He stands fast and suffers long for truth and honour, works hard while others sleep, and shows courage and dares while others run away in fear.
  • Q: Q4. Write the main idea of the poem.
    Ans: The main idea of the poem is that the strength and growth of a nation depend on the hard work, high moral character and virtues of its people, not on wealth. A nation's strength is the fruit of dedicated labour and hard work done with honesty.
  • Q: Q5. Write down the nouns used in the poem.
    Ans: The nouns used in the poem are: gold, men, people, truth, honour, sake, nation, pillars and sky.

Comprehension — B. Gapped Summary: Fill in the gaps with suitable words from the text

  • Q: In this poem the poet tells about the secret of a nation's ______.
    Ans: strength
  • Q: He says that greatness of a nation does not depend upon ______.
    Ans: wealth
  • Q: He says that real strength of a ______ lies in the men of character.
    Ans: nation
  • Q: They ______ their personal interest in the larger interest of their nation.
    Ans: sacrifice
  • Q: They sacrifice their personal interest in the larger interest of their ______.
    Ans: nation
  • Q: They lay the ______ of a nation very deep.
    Ans: foundation
  • Q: Then they take nation to the highest point of ______.
    Ans: sky

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Glossary

  • Q: Q1. What does 'disaster' mean?
    Ans: Disaster means a sudden accident or a natural catastrophe that causes great damage or loss of life.
  • Q: Q2. What does 'hazard' mean?
    Ans: Hazard means a danger or risk.
  • Q: Q3. What does 'anchor' mean?
    Ans: Anchor means a heavy object attached to a cable or chain / to secure firmly in position.
  • Q: Q4. What does 'potential' mean?
    Ans: Potential means having the capacity to develop into something in the future.
  • Q: Q5. What does 'consequences' mean?
    Ans: Consequences means a result of a particular action or situation, often one that is bad or not convenient.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Do you think earthquakes are scary?
    Ans: Yes, earthquakes are scary because there is no guarantee of safety during an earthquake. Buildings can fall, things can fall on people, and an earthquake can cause great damage and loss of life. That is why identifying possible hazards ahead of time and planning in advance can save lives.
  • Q: Q2. Why is the doorway a safe place during an earth quake?
    Ans: The doorway is a safe place during an earthquake because the lesson advises that if you are indoors, you should stand in a doorway or crawl under heavy furniture. Standing in a doorway keeps a person away from windows, outside doors and furniture that can fall on him.
  • Q: Q3. What are some other safe places during an earthquake?
    Ans: Some other safe places during an earthquake are under heavy furniture such as a desk or a table, and in the open outdoors away from buildings, power lines and anything that might fall. If you are in bed, you should hold on and stay there, protecting your head with a pillow.
  • Q: Q4. Does the ground always shake in an earthquake?
    Ans: No, the ground does not always shake in the same way in an earthquake. The lesson shows that safety cannot be guaranteed, so we must always be prepared: stay away from buildings and windows indoors, and stay in the open away from power lines outdoors.
  • Q: Q5. What should you do if you are on a bus trip during an earthquake?
    Ans: If you are on a bus trip during an earthquake, you should stay calm and stay in the bus in a safe place away from buildings, power lines and anything that might fall. After the earthquake, check yourself and others for injuries and provide first aid to anyone who needs it.

Comprehension — B. Choose the correct option

  • Q: Q1. What should you do if you're sitting at a desk when an earthquake strikes?
    Options: Get under the desk. / Run upstairs. / Stay where you are sitting.
    Ans: Get under the desk.
  • Q: Q2. What should you do if you're in car during an earthquake?
    Options: Get out of the car. / Get out of the car and stand under a tree. / Stay in the car.
    Ans: Stay in the car.
  • Q: Q3. What do you do if you're in a stairwell during an earthquake?
    Options: Go up the stairs until you get to the top floor. / Go down the stairs and get out of the building. / Stay where you are, get low and wait.
    Ans: Stay where you are, get low and wait.
  • Q: Q4. What do you think is the level of risk for an earthquake in your city?
    Options: High / Medium / Low
    Ans: Medium
  • Q: Q5. What should your do if you are outdoors when an earthquake hits?
    Options: Stay away from buildings and electricity wires. / Stay near a wall. / Run around for help.
    Ans: Stay away from buildings and electricity wires.

    Ans: Community is a noun. It means a group of people who live in the same place or share the same interests and way of life.
  • Q: Q3. Use dictionary skills to find the meaning of 'rescuer' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Rescuer is a noun. It means a person who saves someone from a dangerous or difficult situation, for example from a damaged building after an earthquake.

    Ans: Predict is a verb. It means to say that something will happen in the future, before it happens.

chapters.title: Unit 5: Democracy

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What is the difference between democracy and monarchy?
    Ans: In a monarchy, one man, the king or queen, rules the country, appoints his own ministers and officers, and the people have no voice in the affairs of the state. In a democracy, the country belongs to the people, who elect their own representatives through elections, and these representatives run the government according to the wishes of the people.
  • Q: Q2. Who has the right to elect the representative of the country in a democratic government?
    Ans: The people of the country have the right to elect the representatives. The lesson says that all people have equal duties and equal rights, so they elect a certain number of persons from among themselves to run the government.
  • Q: Q3. What is the advantage of democratic form of government?
    Ans: In a democracy the government is of the people, for the people and by the people. The representatives rule according to the wishes of the people, and if they do not do so, the people can remove them. All citizens have equal rights and equal duties, and everyone has a voice in the affairs of the state.
  • Q: Q4. What is the disadvantage of monarchy?
    Ans: In a monarchy all power is in the hands of one king. If the king is incompetent, he rules unwisely and spends the government money on his own personal enjoyment instead of the good of his people. The people have no voice in the affairs of the state and cannot remove him.
  • Q: Q5. What do you know about election?
    Ans: Election is the way by which the people choose a certain number of persons from among themselves as their representatives. These representatives run the government of the country. In Pakistan, according to the law of the country, elections are held after every five years for the National Assembly and the provincial assemblies.

Comprehension — B. Fill in the blanks by using context to infer missing words

  • Q: Q1. In Pakistan elections are to be held after every ______ years.
    Ans: five
  • Q: Q2. The President nominates the ______ of Pakistan.
    Ans: Prime Minister
  • Q: Q3. The members of ______ elect the President.
    Ans: provincial assemblies
  • Q: Q4. In monarchy, all powers of the government is in the hands of the ______.
    Ans: king/queen
  • Q: Q5. All people have equal ______ and ______.
    Ans: duties and rights

    Ans: Main idea: In old times almost every country was ruled by a king or a queen, and this form of government is called monarchy. Supporting details: When a king died, his son became king; the king appointed and removed his ministers and officers whenever he wished; a good and wise king made the country progress, but an incompetent king ruled unwisely, spent government money on his own enjoyment, and the people had no voice in the affairs of the state.

lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking — Apologizing (Practice the conversation in pairs)

  • Q: Q1. Develop a conversation between two friends to make and respond to apologies.
    Ans: Friend 1: I am so sorry for being late. I shouldn't have kept you waiting. Please, forgive me. Friend 2: That's all right. Don't worry about it. Friend 1: It's all my fault. I am terribly sorry for the trouble. Friend 2: Never mind. It doesn't matter. We are friends, so forget about it.

Revision Unit 1-5 — H. Identify minimal pairs in the following words

  • Q: Q1. Find the minimal pair for 'sink'.
    Ans: sink — think. The two words differ only in the first sound, /s/ and /th/.
  • Q: Q2. Find the minimal pair for 'sing'.
    Ans: sing — thing. The two words differ only in the first sound, /s/ and /th/.
  • Q: Q3. Find the minimal pair for 'sick'.
    Ans: sick — thick. The two words differ only in the first sound, /s/ and /th/.
  • Q: Q4. Find the minimal pair for 'pass'.

  • Q: Q5. Find the minimal pair for 'fell'.
    Ans: fell — fill. The two words differ only in the middle vowel sound.
  • Q: Q6. Find the minimal pair for 'left'.
    Ans: left — lift. The two words differ only in the middle vowel sound.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — Utilize comparison clues to deduce the meaning of underlined words. Also find the synonyms from thesaurus

  • Q: Q1. She hums continuously, or all the time, and it annoys me. (hums)
    Ans: Deduced meaning: hums means sings with closed lips, making a low continuous musical sound, all the time. Synonym: murmurs.
  • Q: Q2. The dates are listed in chronological order. They start at the beginning and end with the last event. (chronological)
    Ans: Deduced meaning: chronological means arranged in the order of time, starting from the beginning and ending with the last event. Synonym: sequential.
  • Q: Q3. Her animosity or hatred of her sister had divided the family. (animosity)
    Ans: Deduced meaning: animosity means strong hatred or dislike, as the comparison clue 'or hatred' shows. Synonym: hatred / hostility.
  • Q: Q4. Bilal felt remorse or shame for his harsh words. (remorse)
    Ans: Deduced meaning: remorse means deep shame and regret for something wrong that one has done, as the clue 'or shame' shows. Synonym: regret.
  • Q: Q5. This situation is a conundrum - a puzzle for everyone. (conundrum)
    Ans: Deduced meaning: conundrum means a confusing puzzle or a difficult problem, as the clue 'a puzzle' shows. Synonym: puzzle / riddle.

Grammar — Verbs: be, do, have and need as main and as auxiliary verbs (Tell whether the underlined word is main or helping verb)

  • Q: Q1. This old house has no central heating. (has)
    Ans: Main verb. Here 'has' shows possession and carries the main meaning of the sentence itself.
  • Q: Q2. She was forgetting her problems. (was)
    Ans: Helping verb. 'Was' helps the main verb 'forgetting' to form the past continuous tense.
  • Q: Q3. Do you have a glass of water? (have)
    Ans: Main verb. Here 'have' means to possess, and it is the main verb of the sentence.
  • Q: Q4. He is not thinking about his pain. (is)
    Ans: Helping verb. 'Is' helps the main verb 'thinking' to form the present continuous tense.
  • Q: Q5. I have had this computer for three years. (have)
    Ans: Helping verb. The first 'have' helps the main verb 'had' to form the present perfect tense.
  • Q: Q6. They had done their homework. (done)
    Ans: Main verb. 'Done' is the main verb; 'had' is the helping verb that forms the past perfect tense.

Grammar — Linking verbs (Underline the verbs and write whether it is action or linking verb)

  • Q: Q1. She grew into a fine young woman. (grew)
    Ans: Linking verb. 'Grew' links the subject 'She' with the noun phrase 'a fine young woman' and shows no action.
  • Q: Q2. Most people drink coffee or tea every day. (drink)
    Ans: Action verb. 'Drink' shows the action performed by the people.
  • Q: Q3. The vanilla ice cream tasted good. (tasted)
    Ans: Linking verb. 'Tasted' links the ice cream with the adjective 'good'.
  • Q: Q4. He became the first man on the moon. (became)
    Ans: Linking verb. 'Became' links 'He' with the noun phrase 'the first man on the moon'.
  • Q: Q5. The class ate all the burgers at the party. (ate)
    Ans: Action verb. 'Ate' shows the action performed by the class.
  • Q: Q6. A snake will go for anything nearing it. (go)
    Ans: Action verb. 'Go' shows movement/action of the snake, not a link.
  • Q: Q7. The girl looked great in the red dress. (looked)
    Ans: Linking verb. 'Looked' links the girl with the adjective 'great'.
  • Q: Q8. He grew tired of all the negative talk. (grew)
    Ans: Linking verb. 'Grew' links 'He' with the adjective 'tired'.

Grammar — Modal verbs (Fill in the blanks with a modal verb)

  • Q: Q1. ______ I borrow your rubber, please? Yes, of course you ______.
    Ans: May / may (Can / can is also correct)
  • Q: Q2. Don't touch that wire because it ______ be dangerous.
    Ans: may
  • Q: Q3. I ______ swim quite well when I was five years old.
    Ans: could
  • Q: Q4. Sonia ______ practice much if she wants to take part in the race.
    Ans: should
  • Q: Q5. You ______ cook those vegetables because they have already cooked.
    Ans: should not

Grammar — Semi-modal Verbs (Make affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences using could, might, shall, ought and must)

  • Q: Q1. Make an affirmative sentence using 'could'.
    Ans: He could go there.
  • Q: Q2. Make a negative sentence using 'could'.
    Ans: He could not go there.
  • Q: Q3. Make an interrogative sentence using 'could'.
    Ans: Could he go there?
  • Q: Q4. Make an affirmative sentence using 'might'.
    Ans: An accident might happen.
  • Q: Q5. Make a negative sentence using 'might'.
    Ans: An accident might not happen.
  • Q: Q6. Make an interrogative sentence using 'might'.
    Ans: What might happen?
  • Q: Q7. Make an affirmative sentence using 'ought'.
    Ans: You ought to obey your elders.
  • Q: Q8. Make a negative sentence using 'ought'.
    Ans: You ought not to insult anyone.
  • Q: Q9. Make an interrogative sentence using 'ought'.
    Ans: Ought we to obey our elders?
  • Q: Q10. Make an affirmative sentence using 'shall'.
    Ans: We shall go there.
  • Q: Q11. Make a negative sentence using 'shall'.
    Ans: We shall not go there.
  • Q: Q12. Make an interrogative sentence using 'shall'.
    Ans: Shall we go there?
  • Q: Q13. Make an affirmative sentence using 'must'.
    Ans: You must visit here.
  • Q: Q14. Make a negative sentence using 'must'.
    Ans: You must not visit here.
  • Q: Q15. Make an interrogative sentence using 'must'.
    Ans: Must you visit here?

Grammar — Transitive and intransitive verbs: A. Pick out the verbs and tell whether the verb is transitive or intransitive; if transitive, name the object

  • Q: Q1. Bad boys hide their faults.
    Ans: Verb: hide — Transitive verb. Object: their faults.
  • Q: Q2. Some boys threw stones at the frogs.
    Ans: Verb: threw — Transitive verb. Object: stones.
  • Q: Q3. My new watch keeps good time.
    Ans: Verb: keeps — Transitive verb. Object: good time.
  • Q: Q4. The sun rises in the east.
    Ans: Verb: rises — Intransitive verb. It has no object.
  • Q: Q5. The frog jumped out of the pond.
    Ans: Verb: jumped — Intransitive verb. 'Pond' is the object of the preposition 'of', not of the verb.
  • Q: Q6. The birds flew towards west.
    Ans: Verb: flew — Intransitive verb. It has no object.

Grammar — Transitive and intransitive verbs: B. Complete the following by supplying an object

  • Q: Q1. The horse kicked ______.
    Ans: the ball
  • Q: Q2. The teacher punished ______.
    Ans: the student
  • Q: Q3. A shoemaker makes ______.
    Ans: shoes
  • Q: Q4. My brother wrote ______.
    Ans: a letter
  • Q: Q5. He broke ______.
    Ans: a cup

Grammar — Transitive and intransitive verbs: C. Use the following intransitive verbs in sentences of your own

  • Q: Q1. Use 'sneeze' in a sentence.
    Ans: The baby began to sneeze because of the dust.
  • Q: Q2. Use 'agree' in a sentence.
    Ans: We all agree with the teacher.
  • Q: Q3. Use 'appear' in a sentence.
    Ans: The sun will appear from behind the clouds.
  • Q: Q4. Use 'laugh' in a sentence.
    Ans: The children laugh loudly at the joke.
  • Q: Q5. Use 'arrive' in a sentence.
    Ans: The train will arrive at noon.

Revision Unit 1-5 — A. Fill in with the plural form of the irregular nouns in brackets

  • Q: Q1. Karim saw two ______ in the field. (woman)
    Ans: women
  • Q: Q2. Five ______ were playing in my backyard. (child)
    Ans: children
  • Q: Q3. The farmer had seven ______. (goose)
    Ans: geese
  • Q: Q4. Two ______ helped move the load. (man)
    Ans: men

Revision Unit 1-5 — B. Circle the collective noun

  • Q: Q1. The army walked across the land.
    Ans: Collective noun: army.
  • Q: Q2. The troops headed towards the battlefield.
    Ans: Collective noun: troops.
  • Q: Q3. The flock of geese flew over the lake.
    Ans: Collective noun: flock.
  • Q: Q4. The herd moved towards the river.
    Ans: Collective noun: herd.
  • Q: Q5. I bought a bouquet of flowers from the market.
    Ans: Collective noun: bouquet.

Revision Unit 1-5 — C. Underline the correct possessive form for the following animate nouns

  • Q: Q1. The (birds / bird's) nest is in my yard.
    Options: birds / bird's
    Ans: bird's
  • Q: Q2. The (squirrels / squirrel's) tail is bushy.
    Options: squirrels / squirrel's
    Ans: squirrel's
  • Q: Q3. The (childrens / children's) trip to the zoo was fun.
    Options: childrens / children's
    Ans: children's
  • Q: Q4. The (puppys / puppy's) tail wags when he is happy.
    Options: puppys / puppy's
    Ans: puppy's
  • Q: Q5. The (duck's / ducks) home is in the lake.
    Options: duck's / ducks
    Ans: duck's

Revision Unit 1-5 — D. Circle the indefinite pronoun in each sentence below

  • Q: Q1. Make sure to tell everybody about my birthday party.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: everybody.
  • Q: Q2. Everybody wants to win the game.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: Everybody.
  • Q: Q3. She is the one who helps me the most.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: one.
  • Q: Q4. Please tell someone to wash the dishes.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: someone.
  • Q: Q5. Everything we have done has been by the book.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: Everything.

Revision Unit 1-5 — E. Read the following sentences carefully. Tell whether the underlined word is main or helping verb

  • Q: Q1. Do you want to go for picnic? (Do)
    Ans: Helping verb. 'Do' helps the main verb 'want' to form the question.
  • Q: Q2. She has had her dog since 2015. (has)
    Ans: Helping verb. 'Has' helps the main verb 'had' to form the present perfect tense.
  • Q: Q3. He needs to go to the doctor. (needs)
    Ans: Main verb. 'Needs' carries the main meaning of the sentence.
  • Q: Q4. Lubna has been talking for 10 minutes. (has)
    Ans: Helping verb. 'Has' helps to form the present perfect continuous tense.
  • Q: Q5. He was planning a trip to Murree. (was)
    Ans: Helping verb. 'Was' helps the main verb 'planning' to form the past continuous tense.

Revision Unit 1-5 — F. Fill in the blanks with a modal verb

  • Q: Q1. The girl ______ go to the school to learn.
    Ans: should
  • Q: Q2. If you are interested in human life, you ______ study biology.
    Ans: should
  • Q: Q3. He is applying for a job at the university. He ______ get it.
    Ans: may
  • Q: Q4. ______ I have a glass of water, please.
    Ans: May
  • Q: Q5. The players ______ practice in order to win the match.
    Ans: must

Revision Unit 1-5 — G. Underline the verbs and write whether it is action or linking verb

  • Q: Q1. She looks fine. (looks)
    Ans: Linking verb. 'Looks' links 'She' with the adjective 'fine'.
  • Q: Q2. She looked into the street. (looked)
    Ans: Action verb. 'Looked' shows the action of looking into the street.
  • Q: Q3. He is the best soccer player in the world. (is)
    Ans: Linking verb. 'Is' links 'He' with the noun phrase 'the best soccer player in the world'.
  • Q: Q4. She was great in her new performance. (was)
    Ans: Linking verb. 'Was' links 'She' with the adjective 'great'.
  • Q: Q5. He seems confused. (seems)
    Ans: Linking verb. 'Seems' links 'He' with the adjective 'confused'.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — Work in pairs to complete the mind map below. Reflect the opinions in the form of a paragraph

  • Q: Q1. Complete the mind map on: 'Democracy grants every citizen certain rights but these rights cannot be possible without performing certain duties.'
    Ans: Rights of a citizen: the right to vote and elect representatives; the right to express opinions freely; the right to move freely; equal rights in the eyes of the law. Duties of a citizen: to pay taxes; to obey the laws of the country; to vote honestly in elections; to protect and serve the country.
  • Q: Q2. Write a paragraph reflecting the opinions in the mind map.
    Ans: Democracy grants every citizen certain rights, but these rights cannot be possible without performing certain duties. In a democratic country like Pakistan, every citizen has the right to vote, the right to speak freely and the right to live with equality. In return, it is the duty of every citizen to obey the law, to pay taxes honestly and to choose good representatives in elections. The country belongs to the people who live in it, pay taxes and fight for it. If we perform our duties faithfully, our rights will remain safe and our country will make progress.

chapters.title: Unit 6: Little Things

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Reading — Deduce the meaning of the following words

  • Q: Q1. What is the meaning of 'little'?
    Ans: Little means small in size or amount, not big. In the poem, little drops and little grains join together to make very big things.
  • Q: Q2. What is the meaning of 'humble'?
    Ans: Humble means modest and not proud, showing a low estimate of one's own importance, as given in the glossary of the unit.
  • Q: Q3. What is the meaning of 'ocean'?
    Ans: Ocean means a very large sea, a huge body of water. In the poem, little drops of water make the mighty ocean.
  • Q: Q4. What is the meaning of 'ages'?
    Ans: Ages means long periods of time. In the poem, little moments make the mighty ages of eternity.
  • Q: Q5. What is the meaning of 'moments'?
    Ans: Moments means very short periods of time, instants. Little moments, though humble, make the mighty ages.
  • Q: Q6. What is the meaning of 'heaven'?
    Ans: Heaven means the sky above and the beautiful home of happiness where God lives. The poet says little deeds of kindness can make our earth like the heaven above.
  • Q: Q7. What is the meaning of 'deeds'?
    Ans: Deeds means actions or acts done by a person. In the poem, little deeds of kindness make our life happy.
  • Q: Q8. What is the meaning of 'Eden'?
    Ans: Eden means paradise, a place of perfect happiness and beauty. The poet says little deeds of kindness and little words of love make our earth an Eden.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Write the main idea of the poem.
    Ans: The main idea of the poem is the importance of little things in life. Little drops of water make the mighty ocean, little grains of sand make the pleasant land, little moments make the mighty ages of eternity, and little deeds of kindness and little words of love make our earth an Eden, like the heaven above.
  • Q: Q2. How do little deeds of kindness make our life happy?
    Ans: Little deeds of kindness spread love and happiness among people. When we help others and speak kind and loving words, our earth becomes an Eden, like the heaven above, and our life becomes happy and peaceful.
  • Q: Q3. Write about the little act of kindness that you have performed recently.
    Ans: Recently, I performed a little act of kindness. I helped an old woman carry her heavy bag to her home. She was very happy and prayed for me. This small deed cost me nothing, but it made both of us happy and taught me that even a little act of kindness has great value.
  • Q: Q4. Find out the objects of nature in the poem.
    Ans: The objects of nature in the poem are drops of water, grains of sand, the mighty ocean and the pleasant land (the earth). These little things of nature join together to make big and beautiful things.
  • Q: Q5. How can we make the world a better place to live in?
    Ans: We can make the world a better place to live in by doing little deeds of kindness and speaking little words of love. If everyone helps others in small ways and speaks kindly, our earth will become an Eden, like the heaven above.
  • Q: Q6. Write down the nouns used in the poem.
    Ans: The nouns used in the poem are: drops, water, grains, sand, ocean, land, moments, ages, eternity, deeds, kindness, words, love, earth, Eden and heaven.

Comprehension — B. Choose the correct options to fill in the blanks

  • Q: Q1. The poem "little things" is written by ______.
    Options: William Ross Wallace / Ralph Waldo Emerson / Julia Carney / Eliza Cook
    Ans: Julia Carney
  • Q: Q2. Little ______ of sand".
    Options: water / tears / grains / rain
    Ans: grains
  • Q: Q3. Make the mighty ______,
    Options: ocean / world / mountain / sea
    Ans: ocean
  • Q: Q4. And the ______ land.
    Options: sandy / pleasant / mighty / humble
    Ans: pleasant

Comprehension — C. Gapped Summary: Fill in the gaps with suitable words from the text

  • Q: Q1. In this poem the poet explains that how ______ have great importance in life.
    Ans: little things

lessons.notes_html:
Grammar — Adjectives of Quality: A. Pick out the adjectives of quality in the following sentences

  • Q: Q1. The girl has a sweet voice.
    Ans: Adjective of quality: sweet. It describes the quality of the noun 'voice'.
  • Q: Q2. Ali is a fine batsman.
    Ans: Adjective of quality: fine. It describes the quality of the noun 'batsman'.
  • Q: Q3. That is a big house.
    Ans: Adjective of quality: big. It describes the quality (size) of the noun 'house'.
  • Q: Q4. I like red roses.
    Ans: Adjective of quality: red. It describes the quality (colour) of the noun 'roses'.
  • Q: Q5. It is a bright day.
    Ans: Adjective of quality: bright. It describes the quality of the noun 'day'.

Grammar — Adjectives of Quality: B. Pick at least three adjectives of quality from the text

  • Q: Q1. Pick at least three adjectives of quality from the text (the poem).
    Ans: Three adjectives of quality from the poem are: little (little drops of water), mighty (the mighty ocean) and pleasant (the pleasant land). The word 'humble' in 'Humble though they be' is also an adjective of quality.

Grammar — Adjectives of Quantity: C. Pick out the adjectives of quantity in the following sentences

  • Q: Q1. Step back three paces.
    Ans: Adjective of quantity: three. It tells how many paces.
  • Q: Q2. He made several mistakes.
    Ans: Adjective of quantity: several. It tells how many mistakes.
  • Q: Q3. I speak few words.
    Ans: Adjective of quantity: few. It tells how many words.
  • Q: Q4. He is ninety years of age.
    Ans: Adjective of quantity: ninety. It tells the number of years.
  • Q: Q5. Did you get many marks?
    Ans: Adjective of quantity: many. It tells how many marks.

Grammar — Absolute Adjectives (Write whether the following words are absolute adjectives or not)

  • Q: Q1. perfect
    Ans: Yes, 'perfect' is an absolute adjective, because a thing is either perfect or not; it has no comparative or superlative form.
  • Q: Q2. complete
    Ans: Yes, 'complete' is an absolute adjective, because if something is complete, it cannot be more complete or most complete.
  • Q: Q3. red
    Ans: No, 'red' is not an absolute adjective, because it can have degrees, for example redder and reddest.
  • Q: Q4. dead
    Ans: Yes, 'dead' is an absolute adjective, because a person is either dead or alive; it has no comparative or superlative form.
  • Q: Q5. small
    Ans: No, 'small' is not an absolute adjective, because it has comparative and superlative forms: smaller and smallest.
  • Q: Q6. smart
    Ans: No, 'smart' is not an absolute adjective, because it has comparative and superlative forms: smarter and smartest.

Grammar — Regular and irregular Adjectives (Write down the comparative and superlative degrees of the following adjectives. Classify whether the adjective is regular or irregular)

  • Q: Q1. good
    Ans: Comparative: better. Superlative: best. Type: irregular adjective (given in the book).
  • Q: Q2. far
    Ans: Comparative: farther. Superlative: farthest. Type: irregular adjective.
  • Q: Q3. happy
    Ans: Comparative: happier. Superlative: happiest. Type: regular adjective.
  • Q: Q4. little
    Ans: Comparative: less. Superlative: least. Type: irregular adjective.
  • Q: Q5. expensive
    Ans: Comparative: more expensive. Superlative: most expensive. Type: regular adjective.
  • Q: Q6. big
    Ans: Comparative: bigger. Superlative: biggest. Type: regular adjective.
  • Q: Q7. cheap
    Ans: Comparative: cheaper. Superlative: cheapest. Type: regular adjective.
  • Q: Q8. many
    Ans: Comparative: more. Superlative: most. Type: irregular adjective.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Glossary

  • Q: Q1. glad
    Ans: happy
  • Q: Q2. pleasure
    Ans: to enjoy
  • Q: Q3. regards
    Ans: good wishes
  • Q: Q4. disappoint
    Ans: to feel sad

Comprehension A: Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What is an informal letter?
    Ans: An informal letter is a personal letter written to friends and family members in a friendly style and tone. Humera's letter in this unit is an informal letter, because she writes to her friend Hafsa in a warm, personal way to invite her to a birthday party.
  • Q: Q2. Do you know the difference between a formal and informal letter?
    Ans: Yes. A formal letter is written for official purposes, for example to an office or a headmaster, and it uses a serious, polite style. An informal letter is written to people in our immediate social circle, such as friends and relatives, and it uses a friendly style and tone, with greetings like 'My dear Hafsa,' and closings like 'Yours sincerely'.
  • Q: Q3. Why do we need to write a letter?
    Ans: We write a letter to communicate with a person who lives far away in another city or village. Through a letter we can share our news, give information and send messages such as an invitation, just as Humera invites Hafsa to her birthday party and asks her to tell the date and time of her arrival.
  • Q: Q4. Who do you write informal letters to?
    Ans: We write informal letters to the people in our immediate social and academic environment, that is, to our friends, cousins and other family members. In this unit, Humera writes an informal letter to her friend Hafsa.

Comprehension B: Label the parts of the letter with the help of the word bank

    Ans: the middle (d)

  • Q: Q7. Your friend,

  • Q: Q8. Sarah

    Ans: Noun (stress on the first syllable, EXport): Tea is an important export of our country. Verb (stress on the second syllable, exPORT): Pakistan exports rice and cotton to many countries.
  • Q: Q2. import
    Ans: Noun (stress on the first syllable, IMport): The import of machinery has increased this year. Verb (stress on the second syllable, imPORT): We import oil from other countries.
  • Q: Q3. contract
    Ans: Noun (stress on the first syllable, CONtract): The two companies signed a contract for one year. Verb (stress on the second syllable, conTRACT): Metal contracts when it becomes cold.
  • Q: Q4. object
    Ans: Noun (stress on the first syllable, OBject): A strange object was lying on the road. Verb (stress on the second syllable, obJECT): The students did not object to the new timetable.

Grammar — Transitional Devices: Write sentences using the following transitional devices

  • Q: Q1. therefore
    Ans: It was raining heavily; therefore, the birthday party was held inside the house.
  • Q: Q2. either
    Ans: You may either come by bus or by car to attend the party.
  • Q: Q3. further
    Ans: Humera invited a few friends to the party; further, she also invited her cousin Seema from Islamabad.
  • Q: Q4. in contrast
    Ans: Hafsa lives in a busy city; in contrast, her cousin lives in a quiet village.
  • Q: Q5. again
    Ans: Please write to me again and tell me the date and time of your arrival.

Grammar A: Choose the correct preposition

  • Q: Q1. The fridge is between/under the door and the cupboard.
    Options: between / under
    Ans: between
  • Q: Q2. The bin is near/in front of the drawer.
    Options: near / in front of
    Ans: in front of
  • Q: Q3. The microwave is next to/under the window.
    Options: next to / under
    Ans: next to
  • Q: Q4. The door is next to/under the shelf.
    Options: next to / under
    Ans: next to
  • Q: Q5. The clock is in/on the wall.
    Options: in / on
    Ans: on
  • Q: Q6. The chairs are under/next to the table.
    Options: under / next to
    Ans: next to

  • Q: Q1. The curtain is ______ the flush bowl and the bath.
    Ans: between
  • Q: Q2. The flush bowl is ______ the bath.

    Ans: on
  • Q: Q4. The mirror is ______ the washbasin.
    Ans: above
  • Q: Q5. The cupboard is ______ the washbasin.
    Ans: under
  • Q: Q6. The mat is ______ the toilet.
    Ans: near

Grammar C: Fill in the blanks using the prepositions at, in and on

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Glossary

  • Q: Q1. ruins
    Ans: remains
  • Q: Q2. conquer
    Ans: take control of a country
  • Q: Q3. cramped house
    Ans: uncomfortably small or restricted
  • Q: Q4. patterned
    Ans: with a design made from repeated lines, shapes, or colours on the surface
  • Q: Q5. stucco
    Ans: a kind of plaster

Comprehension A: Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Which province of Pakistan is Taxila situated in?
    Ans: Taxila is situated in the Punjab province of Pakistan. The lesson tells us that it is 119 km away from Peshawar and is famous for the ruins of this ancient city, which are spread over an area of sixteen square kilometers.
  • Q: Q2. Name another ancient city that you have heard about.
    Ans: Another ancient city that I have heard about is Mohenjo-daro. Like Taxila, it is famous for the ruins of a very old civilization, and people visit it to learn about the life of people in ancient times.
  • Q: Q3. What do you know about the civilization of Taxila?
    Ans: The civilization of Taxila is almost 2500 years old. Taxila was conquered by the Greek rulers, and during the next 200 years it became a renowned centre of learning, Philosophy and Art. It is divided into three ancient cities: Bhir Mound, Sirkap and Sirsukh.
  • Q: Q4. Propose various suggestions to conserve heritage sites in Pakistan.
    Ans: We can conserve heritage sites in Pakistan by protecting the ruins from damage and keeping these places clean. Nobody should write on the walls or take away old objects from these sites. The government should repair the old buildings, appoint guards to look after them, and punish people who damage them. Schools should arrange visits to these places, as Sakina's school did, so that students learn to value and protect their heritage.
  • Q: Q5. The lesson is in the form of a dialogue. Write the lesson again in the form of a paragraph by using appropriate transitional devices. Describe events in sequential order.
    Ans: One day Sakina came back from school looking very happy. First, she told her father that her school had arranged a visit to Taxila, and her father said that such visits help students learn a lot. Then Sakina asked where Taxila is, so her father told her that it is 119 km away from Peshawar and is famous for the ruins of this ancient city, which are spread over an area of sixteen square kilometers. Next, he told her about its historical background: the civilization of Taxila is almost 2500 years old, it was conquered by the Greek rulers, and during the next 200 years it became a renowned centre of learning, Philosophy and Art. After that, he named its three ancient cities. The earliest city, Bhir Mound, dates back to the sixth century B.C. and had irregular streets and cramped houses; the newer city, Sirkap, on the opposite side of the Tamara Stream, was built in the second century B.C. and was a well planned city; and the third city, Sirsukh, was built by the Kushan kings in the fourth century B.C. and was patterned after Central Asian cities. Finally, her father told her about the endless images of the great saint Gautama Buddha in stone and stucco, and about the museum at Taxila, which has statues, coins, jewellery, seals, beads, silver utensils and carpentry tools, and whose real collection is sculptures made of stone and stucco. In the end, Sakina thanked her father, because now she would be able to enjoy her trip all the more.

Comprehension B: Decide whether the sentences below are fact or opinion

  • Q: Q1. Going to the doctor is scary.
    Ans: Opinion — being scared is a feeling, and feelings may change from person to person.
  • Q: Q2. Abdul Sattar Edhi was a great man.
    Ans: Opinion — calling him a great man is what someone thinks or feels about him; it cannot be proven in the same way for everyone.
  • Q: Q3. Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen.
    Ans: Fact — this is true and can be proven; it does not change, no matter who says it.
  • Q: Q4. Elephants are the largest land mammals.
    Ans: Fact — this is true and can be proven; it does not change, no matter who says it.
  • Q: Q5. The best vacation is going camping.
    Ans: Opinion — the 'best' vacation is what someone thinks or prefers, and it may change from person to person.

Comprehension C: Fill in the blanks to complete the cloze paragraph

  • Q: The civilization of ______ is almost 2500 years old.
    Ans: Taxila
  • Q: The civilization of Taxila is almost 2500 ______ old.
    Ans: years
  • Q: Taxila was ______ by the Greek rulers.
    Ans: conquered
  • Q: Taxila was conquered by the Greek ______.
    Ans: rulers
  • Q: During the next ______ years Taxila became a renowned centre of learning Philosophy and Art.
    Ans: 200
  • Q: During the next 200 years Taxila became ______ centre of learning Philosophy and Art.
    Ans: a renowned
  • Q: During the next 200 years Taxila became a renowned centre of learning ______ and Art.
    Ans: Philosophy
  • Q: It ______ into three ancient cities.
    Ans: is divided
  • Q: It is divided into three ancient ______.
    Ans: cities

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A: Find the meaning of the following words in a dictionary and use them in sentences of your own

  • Q: Q1. suburb
    Ans: Meaning: an area where people live, outside the central part of a city. Sentence: My uncle has built a new house in a quiet suburb of Peshawar.
  • Q: Q2. astonishing
    Ans: Meaning: very surprising. Sentence: Sakina found the history of Taxila astonishing, and said, 'How very astonishing!'
  • Q: Q3. exquisite
    Ans: Meaning: very beautiful and carefully made. Sentence: The museum at Taxila has exquisite sculptures made of stone and stucco.
  • Q: Q4. sculpture
    Ans: Meaning: a figure or work of art made by carving or shaping stone, wood or another hard material. Sentence: The sculptured statues at Taxila tell us about the life and times of Gautama Buddha.
  • Q: Q5. worth seeing
    Ans: Meaning: good and valuable enough to be seen or visited. Sentence: The museum at Taxila has a valuable collection of coins and jewellery, so it is worth seeing.

Grammar A: Fill in the blanks to form adverbs (Adverbs of Manner)

  • Q: slow — ______
    Ans: slowly
  • Q: bad — ______
    Ans: badly
  • Q: angry — ______
    Ans: angrily
  • Q: careful — ______
    Ans: carefully
  • Q: quiet — ______
    Ans: quietly
  • Q: calm — ______
    Ans: calmly
  • Q: perfect — ______
    Ans: perfectly

Grammar: Use the following adverbs of degree in sentences of your own

  • Q: Q1. hardly
    Ans: He was so tired that he could hardly keep his eyes open.
  • Q: Q2. quite
    Ans: The museum at Taxila is quite big and has many valuable things.
  • Q: Q3. enough
    Ans: Sakina is tall enough to reach the top shelf of the cupboard.

Grammar: Circle the adverb of time and underline adverbs of place in the sentences below

  • Q: Q1. He's going to Germany next week.
    Ans: Adverb of time: next week. Adverb of place: Germany (he is going to Germany).
  • Q: Q2. The cat was hiding under the table yesterday.
    Ans: Adverb of time: yesterday. Adverb of place: under the table.
  • Q: Q3. There was a rainstorm in Lahore during the night.
    Ans: Adverb of time: during the night. Adverb of place: in Lahore.
  • Q: Q4. The other day when she saw me waiting, she ran towards me.
    Ans: Adverb of time: the other day. Adverb of place: towards me.
  • Q: Q5. The plane had to fly through a heavy storm last month.
    Ans: Adverb of time: last month. Adverb of place: through a heavy storm.
  • Q: Q6. They shifted to a house nearby last month.
    Ans: Adverb of time: last month. Adverb of place: nearby (they shifted to a house nearby).

Grammar: Put the adverb of frequency on the right place

  • Q: Q1. He listens to the radio. (often)
    Ans: He often listens to the radio.
  • Q: Q2. They read a book. (sometimes)
    Ans: They sometimes read a book.
  • Q: Q3. Palwasha gets angry. (never)
    Ans: Palwasha never gets angry.
  • Q: Q4. Tauseeq is very friendly. (usually)
    Ans: Tauseeq is usually very friendly.
  • Q: Q5. My grandmother goes for a walk in the evening. (always)
    Ans: My grandmother always goes for a walk in the evening.

Grammar C: Underline the adverbs of reason in the following sentences

  • Q: Q1. The students bullied her, she therefore, left college.
    Ans: The adverb of reason is 'therefore'.
  • Q: Q2. The teacher is ill and is therefore unable to come to school.
    Ans: The adverb of reason is 'therefore'.
  • Q: Q3. Madiha was neglected by the teachers, hence, she failed in the exam.
    Ans: The adverb of reason is 'hence'.
  • Q: Q4. Asad is very bright, he often gets awards for his talent.
    Ans: There is no adverb of reason in this sentence. 'Often' is an adverb of frequency, not of reason.
  • Q: Q5. The bell rang so he left the school.
    Ans: The adverb of reason is 'so'.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Why couldn't Huma reply Asma earlier?
    Ans: Huma could not reply to Asma earlier because she was busy with her exams. She wrote the letter on 2nd March, 2017, after her exams were over and she was free.
  • Q: Q2. What profession does Huma want to choose? Why?
    Ans: Huma wants to become a nurse. She feels that nursing is a very respectable profession, and she has always had a passion to serve the sick and the ailing. She wants to work day and night to bring joy and comfort to the sick and the suffering.
  • Q: Q3. Which profession do you want to take up? Why?
    Ans: I want to become a teacher. Teaching is a very respectable profession, and a teacher builds the future of the nation by educating children. I love reading and explaining things to others, so I want to spread knowledge and help my students become good and successful citizens.
  • Q: Q4. What are the influences that shape children's choice of career?
    Ans: Children's choice of career is shaped by many influences. Parents and elder brothers and sisters often advise them, as Huma's Baji advised her to join the Computer Science group and her Abboo wished her to join the College of Home Economics. Teachers, friends, personal interest and passion, and the needs of society also shape a child's choice of career.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — Find the meaning of the following words in the dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviation used. Consult a thesaurus and find out the synonyms

  • Q: Q1. command
    Ans: Meaning: an order given to a person. Part of speech: noun (n.); it is also used as a verb. Synonym: order.
  • Q: Q2. free
    Ans: Meaning: not busy; having time to do something, as Huma says, 'Now I am free.' Part of speech: adjective (adj.). Synonym: available, unoccupied.
  • Q: Q3. truly
    Ans: Meaning: really and sincerely, as in the closing of a letter, 'Yours truly.' Part of speech: adverb (adv.). Synonym: sincerely, really.
  • Q: Q4. suffering
    Ans: Meaning: the state of undergoing pain, trouble etc. Part of speech: noun (n.). Synonym: pain, hardship.
  • Q: Q5. choice
    Ans: Meaning: the act of choosing between two or more things; the thing chosen. Part of speech: noun (n.). Synonym: selection, option.
  • Q: Q6. sick
    Ans: Meaning: ill; not well in health, as Huma wants to serve the sick and the ailing. Part of speech: adjective (adj.). Synonym: ill, unwell.

Grammar — A. Complete the sentences with the correct verb forms of present simple or continuous

  • Q: Q1. It ______ here in summer? (rain)
    Ans: rains
  • Q: Q2. Your English ______ better. (get)
    Ans: is getting
  • Q: Q3. Where's Sara? She ______ now. (sleep)
    Ans: is sleeping
  • Q: Q4. Well, goodnight. I ______ to bed. (go)
    Ans: am going
  • Q: Q5. Water ______ at 100°C. (boil)
    Ans: boils

Grammar — B. Put each verb in brackets into either the present simple or the present continuous

  • Q: Dear Uncle Fazal, I ______ (write) to tell you how I am getting on in my first term at School.
    Ans: am writing
  • Q: I ______ (get on) in my first term at School.
    Ans: am getting on
  • Q: Actually, I ______ (really enjoy) myself!
    Ans: am really enjoying
  • Q: I ______ (study) quite hard as well, but at the moment I am spending a lot of time just making friends.
    Ans: study
  • Q: At the moment I ______ (spend) a lot of time just making friends.
    Ans: am spending
  • Q: I ______ (stay) with my friend Zaitoon, and I am looking for someplace of my own to live.
    Ans: am staying
  • Q: I ______ (look for) someplace of my own to live.
    Ans: am looking for
  • Q: Everything ______ (cost) a lot here, and I am saving to buy a winter coat.
    Ans: costs
  • Q: I ______ (save) to buy a winter coat.
    Ans: am saving
  • Q: It ______ (get) really cold here in the evenings.
    Ans: is getting

Grammar — C. Write your daily routine using simple present tense

  • Q: Q1. Write your daily routine using simple present tense.
    Ans: I get up early in the morning. I say my prayers and take a bath. Then I eat my breakfast and go to school. I attend my classes and learn my lessons. In the afternoon I come back home and take rest for some time. Then I do my homework and play with my friends in the evening. At night I eat dinner with my family and go to bed early.

Grammar — C. Complete the sentences using am / is / are and one of the verbs below (washing, cooking, playing, building, swimming, snowing, taking, watching, coming, doing)

  • Q: Q1. I can't talk now. I ______ the dishes.
    Ans: am washing
  • Q: Q2. Listen to Jim. He ______ the guitar.
    Ans: is playing
  • Q: Q3. It ______ so we can go skiing.
    Ans: is snowing
  • Q: Q4. Look at Jill. She ______ in the river.
    Ans: is swimming
  • Q: Q5. They ______ a new house.
    Ans: are building
  • Q: Q6. Someone ______. I can smell the food.
    Ans: is cooking
  • Q: Q7. Hurry. The bus ______.
    Ans: is coming
  • Q: Q8. They ______ their exercises so they can lose weight.
    Ans: are doing
  • Q: Q9. I can't answer the phone. I ______ a shower.
    Ans: am taking
  • Q: Q10. Danish and Jaffar ______ the football on TV.
    Ans: are watching

Grammar — D. Form sentences in the present continuous tense

  • Q: Q1. I sit on a chair.
    Ans: I am sitting on a chair.
  • Q: Q2. They play football.
    Ans: They are playing football.
  • Q: Q3. It rains.
    Ans: It is raining.
  • Q: Q4. Annie writes a letter.
    Ans: Annie is writing a letter.
  • Q: Q5. Bashir reads a book.
    Ans: Bashir is reading a book.

lessons.notes_html:
Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. If you write a letter to the Editor of a Daily Newspaper, how will you write the inside address and salutation?
    Ans: For a formal letter, the inside address is the name and address of the person to whom the letter is addressed, written at the top. For the Editor it is written as: 'The Editor, Daily Mashriq, Peshawar.' The salutation of such a formal letter is 'Dear Sir,' with a comma after the name or title.
  • Q: Q2. Is there a post office near your house? Have you ever been there?
    Ans: Yes, there is a post office near my house. Yes, I have been there many times. I go there to post letters, to buy stamps and envelopes, and to send parcels to my relatives in other cities.
  • Q: Q3. Write down your name and address on an envelope.
    Ans: The name and address are written clearly in the middle of the envelope, for example: To, Atif Khan, Govt. High School No. 1, Bannu City.

Vocabulary — Underline the phrases through keywords and match them with relevant pictures

  • Q: Q1. The dinosaur is holding a large egg.
    Ans: Phrase: 'a large egg'. It matches the picture of the dinosaur.

  • Q: Q3. I have a great idea.
    Ans: Phrase: 'a great idea'. It matches the picture of the boy who has an idea, shown with a lighted bulb above his head.
  • Q: Q4. My baby likes playing with toys.
    Ans: Phrase: 'playing with toys'. It matches the picture of the mother with her baby.
  • Q: Q5. The girl is sitting near the fire because it's very cold.
    Ans: Phrases: 'sitting near the fire' and 'very cold'. It matches the picture of the girl sitting near the fire.
  • Q: Q6. The dinosaur is hatching from an egg.
    Ans: Phrase: 'hatching from an egg'. It matches the picture of the dinosaur hatching from an egg.

chapters.title: Unit 11: The Wolf Cub

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Glossary

  • Q: Q1. infant
    Ans: A very young child or baby.
  • Q: Q2. warned
    Ans: Inform someone in advance of a possible danger / situation.
  • Q: Q3. tremble
    Ans: Shake as a result of anxiety, excitement, fear.
  • Q: Q4. reign
    Ans: The period of rule of a monarch.
  • Q: Q5. terror
    Ans: Extreme fear.
  • Q: Q6. thunderous
    Ans: Speak loudly and forcefully or angrily.
  • Q: Q7. hurled
    Ans: Thrown with great force.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Who are the main characters of the story?
    Ans: The main characters are Mowgli, the little boy who was found as an infant in the jungle and brought up by the Mother Wolf, and Cheeto, the strong tiger who did not like Mowgli. The whole story turns on Cheeto's wish to harm Mowgli and on Mowgli's plan to save himself.
  • Q: Q2. Are there any minor characters in the story? If so who are they?
    Ans: Yes, there are minor characters. They are the Mother Wolf, who brought Mowgli up just as she had brought up her own cubs, Bhaloo the bear, Bhagera the panther, Kaa the snake, Mowgli's many monkey friends, and the eight wild bulls who charged at Cheeto.
  • Q: Q3. Is there any moral in the story? If so what is it?
    Ans: Yes. The theme of the story, as given in the book, is friendship and cooperation. Mowgli could not defeat the strong tiger alone, but with the help of his friend Kaa and the wild bulls he ended Cheeto's reign of terror. The moral is that true friends help one another, and together even a strong enemy can be faced.
  • Q: Q4. With whose help did Mowgli kill Cheeto?
    Ans: Mowgli killed Cheeto with the help of his friend Kaa and the eight wild bulls. That evening, with Kaa's help, he gathered eight wild bulls with the longest and sharpest horns. On Mowgli's signal the bulls charged down the slope, pierced Cheeto with their horns and flung him to his death.
  • Q: Q5. Which character do you dislike and why?
    Ans: I dislike Cheeto, the tiger. He was strong and did not like Mowgli. He always waited for a chance to harm the boy, and he went around telling everyone that he wanted to kill Mowgli. His reign was a reign of terror for the jungle.
  • Q: Q6. Who is your favourite character in the story and why?
    Ans: My favourite character is Mowgli. He is brave and clever. When Bhaloo warned him that Cheeto wanted to kill him, he did not panic; he said he could protect himself and made a wise plan to counter-attack with the help of the wild bulls. He also loves his jungle friends, who love him very much.
  • Q: Q7. What is the setting of the story?
    Ans: The setting is the thick of a jungle. Mowgli plays there with the wolf cubs and the other animals, and Cheeto spends most of his time on a slope in the mountains, far from Mowgli's cave, where the final attack takes place.

Comprehension — B. Write in the space provided, the category each of the sentence falls in i.e. character, setting or problem

  • Q: Q1. Mowgli and Bhaloo.
    Ans: Character — Mowgli and Bhaloo are characters of the story.
  • Q: Q2. "Mowgli, Cheeto is in a terrible temper. He is going around telling everyone that he wants to kill you."
    Ans: Problem — Cheeto wants to kill Mowgli, and this is the problem that Mowgli has to solve.
  • Q: Q3. In the thick of a jungle.
    Ans: Setting — the story takes place in the thick of a jungle.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — A. Find the meaning of the following words in a dictionary and tell which part of speech they are

  • Q: Q1. pierced
    Ans: Verb. It means made a hole in something or went through it with a sharp point. In the story, the bulls pierced Cheeto with their horns.
  • Q: Q2. signal
    Ans: Noun. It means a sign, sound or action that gives an order or a message. In the story, Mowgli lifted up his hands, brought them down and shouted "CHARGE" as the signal for the bulls to attack.
  • Q: Q3. flung
    Ans: Verb. It is the past form of fling and means thrown with great force. In the story, the bulls flung Cheeto with the momentum of their run.
  • Q: Q4. momentum
    Ans: Noun. It means the force that a moving body gains because of its movement. The running bulls had so much momentum that they hurled Cheeto to his death.
  • Q: Q5. announced
    Ans: Verb. It is the past form of announce and means made something known to everyone. Mowgli and the bulls proudly went back to announce Cheeto's end to the jungle folks.
  • Q: Q6. circled
    Ans: Verb. It is the past form of circle and means moved round in a circle. As per the plan, Mowgli and the bulls circled the mountain, unnoticed by the slumbering tiger.

Grammar — Simple Future Tense

  • Q: Q1. I will see — give the negative, interrogative and interrogative negative forms.
    Ans: Negative: I won't see. Interrogative: Will I see? Interrogative Negative: Won't I see?
  • Q: Q2. I shall see — give the negative, interrogative and interrogative negative forms.
    Ans: Negative: I shall not see. Interrogative: Shall I see? Interrogative Negative: Shall I not see?
  • Q: Q3. You will see — give the negative, interrogative and interrogative negative forms.
    Ans: Negative: You won't see. Interrogative: Will you see? Interrogative Negative: Won't you see?
  • Q: Q4. He will see — give the negative, interrogative and interrogative negative forms.
    Ans: Negative: He won't see. Interrogative: Will he see? Interrogative Negative: Won't he see?
  • Q: Q5. We will see — give the negative, interrogative and interrogative negative forms.
    Ans: Negative: We won't see. Interrogative: Will we see? Interrogative Negative: Won't we see?
  • Q: Q6. We shall see — give the negative, interrogative and interrogative negative forms.
    Ans: Negative: We shall not see. Interrogative: Shall we see? Interrogative Negative: Shall we not see?
  • Q: Q7. They will see — give the negative, interrogative and interrogative negative forms.
    Ans: Negative: They won't see. Interrogative: Will they see? Interrogative Negative: Won't they see?

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — A. In your notebooks write as many details as you know about the following characters and what is happening in the story

  • Q: Q1. Mowgli
    Ans: Mowgli is a little human boy. As an infant he was found by the Mother Wolf in the jungle, and she brought him up just as she had brought up her own cubs, so he is called the wolf cub. He plays with all the animals of the jungle and has many friends: Bhaloo the bear, Bhagera the panther, Kaa the snake and many monkeys. He has always been warned to stay away from the Tiger's territory. He is brave and intelligent: when he learns that Cheeto wants to kill him, he makes a plan, gathers eight wild bulls with Kaa's help and defeats Cheeto.
  • Q: Q2. Cheeto
    Ans: Cheeto is the tiger in the story. He is strong and is not a friend of Mowgli; he does not like the boy and always waits for a chance to harm him. He spends most of his time on a slope in the mountains, far from Mowgli's cave. In a terrible temper he goes around telling everyone that he wants to kill Mowgli, and his rule is called a reign of terror. In the end the charging bulls pierce him with their horns and hurl him to his death.

Writing — B. Write a story of your own choice using the elements of a story

  • Q: Q1. Write a story of your own choice using the elements of a story.
    Ans: Model story — 'The Lost Lamb'. Characters: Bilal, a young shepherd boy, and his faithful dog Sheru. Setting: A green valley near a forest, in the evening. Beginning: One evening Bilal was bringing his sheep home when he counted them and found that one little lamb was missing. Dark clouds were gathering and he could hear wolves in the forest. Middle: Bilal did not lose courage. He took his stick and went back into the forest with Sheru. Sheru sniffed the ground and ran ahead, barking. At last they found the lamb trapped in a thorny bush, trembling with fear. Bilal freed it gently and carried it on his shoulders. End: Bilal, Sheru and the lamb reached home safely before the rain began, and his father praised him for his courage and care. Moral: We should never leave our duty in fear; courage, quick thinking and a faithful friend help us in every trouble.
