lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar B — Punctuate the following newspaper article

  • Q: Q1. Punctuate the newspaper article about the elephant, using full stop, comma, question mark, quotation marks and exclamation mark.
    Ans: The elephant is the Earth's largest land animal, although the Asian elephant is slightly smaller than its African cousin. Asian elephants can be identified by their smaller, rounded ears. Elephant ears radiate heat to help keep these large animals cool, but sometimes that isn't enough. Elephants are fond of water and enjoy showering by sucking water into their trunks and spraying it all over themselves. Elephants eat roots, grasses, fruit and bark. They eat a lot of these things. An adult elephant can consume up to 300 pounds of food in a single day.

Revision Unit 16–20 A — Change the following active sentences into passive voice

  • Q: Q1. I did not beat her.
    Ans: She was not beaten by me.
  • Q: Q2. Mother made a cake yesterday.
    Ans: A cake was made by Mother yesterday.
  • Q: Q3. The brother teased the sister.
    Ans: The sister was teased by the brother.
  • Q: Q4. The tiger was chasing the deer.
    Ans: The deer was being chased by the tiger.
  • Q: Q5. She has written a novel.
    Ans: A novel has been written by her.

Revision Unit 16–20 B — Sentences are given in the direct speech. Change them into indirect speech

  • Q: Q1. He said, "I have got a toothache".
    Ans: He said that he had got a toothache.
  • Q: Q2. Mano said, "I am very busy now".
    Ans: Mano said that she was very busy then.
  • Q: Q3. She said, "I am going to school."
    Ans: She said that she was going to school.
  • Q: Q4. Afia says, "My father is an Engineer."
    Ans: Afia says that her father is an Engineer.
  • Q: Q5. She said to me, "You are my only friend."
    Ans: She told me that I was her only friend.

Revision Unit 16–20 C — Rewrite and punctuate the sentences below

  • Q: Q1. What are you going to do today Kamal (rewrite and punctuate)
    Ans: What are you going to do today, Kamal?
  • Q: Q2. What an amazing goal (rewrite and punctuate)
    Ans: What an amazing goal!
  • Q: Q3. I am going to go home if I finish my schoolwork on time (rewrite and punctuate)
    Ans: I am going to go home if I finish my schoolwork on time.
  • Q: Q4. I hate it (rewrite and punctuate)
    Ans: I hate it.
  • Q: Q5. When are you going to go shopping in Saddar bazaar (rewrite and punctuate)
    Ans: When are you going to go shopping in Saddar Bazaar?

Revision Unit 16–20 D — Complete the conditional sentences (Type 1) by inserting verbs

  • Q: If it rains, you will ______.
    Ans: stay at home
  • Q: If Sadaf is late again I will ______.
    Ans: go without her
  • Q: If you don't hurry, you will ______.
    Ans: be late
  • Q: If I have time, I'll finish ______.
    Ans: my homework
  • Q: If you drop that glass, it will ______.
    Ans: break

mcqs.q: According to the punctuated elephant article, what is the elephant?
options: The smallest land animal in Asia
An animal found only in Africa
mcqs.why: Grammar B in the notes begins the punctuated article: The elephant is the Earth's largest land animal.

mcqs.q: How does the Asian elephant compare with its African cousin?
options: It is slightly smaller than its African cousin
It is slightly larger than its African cousin
It is exactly the same size and shape
It has much larger, pointed ears
mcqs.why: Grammar B in the notes says the Asian elephant is slightly smaller than its African cousin, although the elephant is the largest land animal.

mcqs.q: How can Asian elephants be identified, according to the article?
options: By their long tails and stripes
By the colour of their trunks
mcqs.why: Grammar B in the notes says Asian elephants can be identified by their smaller, rounded ears.

mcqs.q: Why do elephant ears radiate heat, according to the article?
options: To help them hear distant sounds
To help keep these large animals cool
mcqs.why: Grammar B in the notes says elephant ears radiate heat to help keep these large animals cool, though sometimes that is not enough.

mcqs.q: How do elephants shower, according to the article?
options: By rolling in rivers all day
By sucking water into their trunks and spraying it all over themselves
By pouring water with their ears
mcqs.why: Grammar B in the notes says elephants enjoy showering by sucking water into their trunks and spraying it all over themselves.

mcqs.q: How much food can an adult elephant consume in a single day?
options: Only roots and bark, nothing else
mcqs.why: Grammar B in the notes says an adult elephant can consume up to 300 pounds of food in a single day, eating roots, grasses, fruit and bark.

mcqs.q: Change to passive voice: 'I did not beat her.'
options: She was not beaten by me.
She did not beat by me.
Her was not beaten by I.
She is not beat by me yesterday.
mcqs.why: Revision A in the notes gives the passive form as: She was not beaten by me, for I did not beat her.

mcqs.q: Change to passive voice: 'Mother made a cake yesterday.'
options: A cake is made by Mother tomorrow.
A cake was made by Mother yesterday.
Mother was made by a cake yesterday.
A cake has made by Mother yesterday.
mcqs.why: Revision A in the notes gives the passive form as: A cake was made by Mother yesterday.

mcqs.q: Change to passive voice: 'She has written a novel.'
options: A novel was wrote by her.
She has been written by a novel.
A novel has been written by her.
A novel is written by her yesterday.
mcqs.why: Revision A in the notes gives the passive form as: A novel has been written by her, keeping the present perfect in passive.

mcqs.q: Change to indirect speech: He said, 'I have got a toothache.'
options: He said that he had got a toothache.
He said that I have got a toothache.
He says that he has got a toothache now.
He told that he will get a toothache.
mcqs.why: Revision B in the notes changes it to: He said that he had got a toothache, shifting have got to had got in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: Change to indirect speech: Mano said, 'I am very busy now.'
options: Mano said that I am very busy now.
Mano said that she is very busy now.
Mano says that she was very busy then.
Mano said that she was very busy then.
mcqs.why: Revision B in the notes changes it to: Mano said that she was very busy then, changing am to was and now to then.

mcqs.q: Change to indirect speech: Afia says, 'My father is an Engineer.'
options: Afia said that her father was an Engineer.
Afia says that her father is an Engineer.
Afia says that my father is an Engineer.
Afia told that her father will be an Engineer.
mcqs.why: Revision B in the notes keeps says in the present: Afia says that her father is an Engineer, so the tense does not shift back.

mcqs.q: Rewrite and punctuate: 'What are you going to do today Kamal'
options: What are you going to do today, Kamal?
What are you going to do today Kamal.
What are you going to do today, Kamal!
What, are you going to do today Kamal?
mcqs.why: Revision C in the notes punctuates it as a question with a comma before the name: What are you going to do today, Kamal?

mcqs.q: Rewrite and punctuate: 'What an amazing goal'
mcqs.why: Revision C in the notes punctuates this exclamation as: What an amazing goal! with an exclamation mark.

mcqs.q: Complete the Type 1 conditional from Revision D: 'If you drop that glass, it will ___.'
mcqs.why: Revision D in the notes completes the conditional as: If you drop that glass, it will break.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — Write an essay on causes and effects of over population by using the given target language and lexical variation

  • Q: Q1. Write an essay on causes and effects of over population by using the given target language and lexical variation.
    Ans: Causes and Effects of Overpopulation: Overpopulation means too many people living in a place. Our cities are overcrowded and teeming with people. Owing to poverty and unemployment in the villages, people leave their homes and come to the cities for work. As a result, the population of the cities is growing day by day. One effect of this is that the cities have become too dense a population to live in comfortably. Houses are costly and many inhabitants have no proper place to live. Consequently, streets are crowded with people and roads are crawling with cars, so traffic jams have become a daily problem. Another effect of overcrowding is dirt and disease; too many people create rubbish and pollution, and hence sickness spreads quickly. For this reason, life in the cities has become restless and hard. Therefore, we must control the growing population, and the government should provide jobs and facilities in the villages. Thus the rush towards the cities will slow down and city life will become peaceful again.

mcqs.q: What does overpopulation mean, according to the model essay?
options: Too few people living in villages
Too many people living in a place
Too many cars on city roads only
Too many houses in a city only
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes begins: Overpopulation means too many people living in a place, and our cities are overcrowded.

mcqs.q: How are the cities described at the start of the model essay?
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes describes the cities as overcrowded and teeming with people.

mcqs.q: Why do people leave the villages for the cities, according to the essay?
options: Owing to poverty and unemployment in the villages, they come to the cities for work
Owing to traffic jams in the villages
Because houses are cheaper in cities
Because villages have too many jobs
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes gives poverty and unemployment in the villages as the cause, with people coming to cities for work.

mcqs.q: What happens to the population of the cities as a result, according to the essay?
options: It is falling day by day
It is growing day by day
It moves back to the villages
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes says as a result the population of the cities is growing day by day.

mcqs.q: What housing effect of overcrowding is given in the essay?
options: Houses are costly and many inhabitants have no proper place to live
Every inhabitant has a large house
Houses are free for new arrivals
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes says houses are costly and many inhabitants have no proper place to live in the overcrowded cities.

mcqs.q: What traffic effect of overcrowding is given in the essay?
options: Streets are crowded, roads are crawling with cars, and traffic jams are a daily problem
Roads are empty and travel is fast
Traffic jams happen only once a year
Streets are closed to all cars
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes says streets are crowded and roads crawling with cars, so traffic jams have become a daily problem.

mcqs.q: What health effect of overcrowding is given in the essay?
options: Dirt and disease; rubbish and pollution make sickness spread quickly
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes gives dirt and disease as an effect: too many people create rubbish and pollution, and sickness spreads quickly.

mcqs.q: How is city life described as a result of overcrowding in the essay?
options: Restless and hard, too dense a population to live in comfortably
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes says life in the cities has become restless and hard and too dense to live in comfortably.

mcqs.q: What must be done about the growing population, according to the essay?
options: We must control the growing population
We must increase the population faster
We must move all villagers to cities
We must close all village schools
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes concludes we must control the growing population to make city life peaceful again.

mcqs.q: What should the government do, according to the essay?
options: Provide more cars for city roads
Provide jobs and facilities in the villages so the rush to cities slows down
Build only costly houses in cities
Stop all work in the villages
mcqs.why: The model essay in the notes says the government should provide jobs and facilities in the villages, thus slowing the rush towards the cities.
